---
title: "Step 2. Score the likelihood"
description: "Score six likelihood dimensions at design."
---

Do this in [Phase 2, design](../02-design/index.qmd), once the data and the method are settled. If
an impact dimension scored 4, go to [Business Critical analysis](../08-business-critical/index.qmd).

Score how easily the analysis could be wrong. Score it in the [Analytical Assurance Decision Tool spreadsheet]({{< var decision-tool >}}), which describes each
dimension at each level. Opening it needs an NHSBSA account with access to the Analytical Quality and Assurance site.

## What you do

- Score each of the six likelihood dimensions in the tool, from Level 1 to Level 4: data
  complexity, analytical complexity, assumptions and proxies, novelty, manual intervention, and
  documentation and reproducibility.
- Score against the tool's description for each level, not the dimension's name. Treat the methods
  it names as examples.
- Score the process as it is now, not as it will be after any planned automation.
- Take the highest single score as your likelihood score.

Your likelihood score is the other side of the matrix. Read your level where the two meet.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-assurance-level-matrix.qmd >}}

## Outputs of this step

Record these in the Specification:

- The score for each dimension, and your highest single score.

## What you do next

Read your level from your two scores in [Step 3. Read your level](read-your-level.qmd).
